title: Luke Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Luke 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea
John preaching the baptism of repentance
The voice crying in the wilderness
The people asking what they shall do
questions.correctAnswer: Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea
questions.explanation: Luke 3:1 lists Pontius Pilate as governor of Judaea before mentioning John preaching and other events.

questions.question: Who was governor of Judaea during the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar's reign?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:1 states Pontius Pilate was governor of Judaea at that time.

questions.question: Where did the word of God come unto John the son of Zacharias?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:2 says the word of God came unto John in the wilderness.

questions.question: What was John preaching about in the country around Jordan?
options: Baptism of repentance for the remission of sins
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism of repentance for the remission of sins
questions.explanation: Luke 3:3 states John preached baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

questions.question: Which prophet's words are quoted in Luke 3 about preparing the way of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:4 quotes the book of the words of Esaias the prophet.

questions.question: According to Luke 3, what shall every valley do?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:5 says every valley shall be filled.

questions.question: What will all flesh see, according to Luke 3?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:6 states all flesh shall see the salvation of God.

questions.question: What did John call the multitude that came to be baptized?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:7 says John called the multitude a generation of vipers.

questions.question: What did John say to the people about relying on Abraham as their father?
options: God can raise up children of Abraham from stones
They should not fear God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God can raise up children of Abraham from stones
questions.explanation: Luke 3:8 states God is able to raise children unto Abraham from stones.

questions.question: What is laid unto the root of the trees according to John?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:9 says the axe is laid unto the root of the trees.

questions.question: What did the people ask John after his warnings?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:10 records the people asking John what they should do.

questions.question: If a person has two coats, what did John say they should do?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:11 says he who has two coats should impart to him that has none.

questions.question: Publicans came to John asking what they should do to be baptized.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:12 states publicans came to be baptized and asked John what they should do.

questions.question: John told the publicans to collect as much tax as they could to be baptized.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:13 says John told them to exact no more than that which is appointed, not to collect as much as possible.

questions.question: Luke 3 says that John baptized Jesus in the Jordan river.
questions.explanation: The text in Luke 3:1-13 does not mention John baptizing Jesus.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did John the Baptist say to the soldiers who asked him what they should do?
options: Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages.
Exact no more than that which is appointed to you.
Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance.
Prepare ye the way of the Lord.
questions.correctAnswer: Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages.
questions.explanation: This is the instruction given by John the Baptist to the soldiers in Luke 3:14, emphasizing integrity and contentment.

questions.question: What does Luke 3:15 promise will happen if someone is in expectation of the Christ, as indicated in verse 3:15?
options: They shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.
They shall see the salvation of God.
They will be reproved for their sins.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall see the salvation of God.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:6 states that all flesh shall see the salvation of God, which connects to the expectation of the Christ mentioned in verse 15.

questions.question: Who will baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire, according to John the Baptist?
questions.explanation: In Luke 3:16, John refers to one mightier than himself, who is Jesus, indicating that He will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire.

questions.question: What happens to the chaff, according to Luke 3:17?
options: It is gathered into the garner.
It is burned with unquenchable fire.
questions.correctAnswer: It is burned with unquenchable fire.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:17 states that the chaff will be burned with fire unquenchable, illustrating the judgment that follows the gathering of the wheat.

questions.question: What does Luke 3:18 indicate about John the Baptist's message?
options: He preached many other things in his exhortation.
He foretold the coming of Herod.
questions.correctAnswer: He preached many other things in his exhortation.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:18 highlights that John preached various exhortations, indicating a broader message beyond just baptism and repentance.

questions.question: What led to John being imprisoned according to Luke 3:20?
options: His reproving of Herod for Herodias.
questions.correctAnswer: His reproving of Herod for Herodias.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:19 explains that John was reproved Herod for Herodias, which ultimately led to his imprisonment.

questions.question: What significant event occurred when Jesus was baptized, as described in Luke 3:21?
options: The Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove.
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:22 describes how the Holy Ghost descended upon Jesus in the form of a dove during His baptism, signifying divine approval.

questions.question: What did the voice from heaven declare about Jesus in Luke 3:22?
options: He is the Son of God.
He is my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
He is the King of Kings.
questions.correctAnswer: He is my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
questions.explanation: Luke 3:22 records the voice from heaven affirming Jesus as God's beloved Son, which signifies His divine nature and mission.

questions.question: How old was Jesus when He began His ministry, according to Luke 3:23?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:23 states that Jesus began His ministry at about thirty years of age, marking the start of His public life.

questions.question: What does Luke 3:10 reveal about the people's response to John's preaching?
options: They asked, 'What shall we do then?'
questions.correctAnswer: They asked, 'What shall we do then?'
questions.explanation: In Luke 3:10, the people were responsive to John's message, seeking guidance on how to act upon his teachings.

questions.question: According to Luke 3:13, what did John tell the publicans regarding their duties?
options: To exact no more than that which is appointed to them.
questions.correctAnswer: To exact no more than that which is appointed to them.
questions.explanation: In Luke 3:13, John instructs the publicans to be honest in their dealings and not overcharge, promoting integrity.

questions.question: What does John the Baptist's exhortation teach about contentment and integrity?
options: We should always seek better wages.
We should act justly and be content with what we have.
We should be ruthless in our professions.
We should rely on others for our needs.
questions.correctAnswer: We should act justly and be content with what we have.
questions.explanation: John's teachings emphasize the importance of integrity in actions and contentment, particularly in Luke 3:14, where he advises soldiers to be content with their wages.

questions.question: Is it true that the chaff will be burned with unquenchable fire?
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in Luke 3:17, which states that the chaff will be burned with fire unquenchable, indicating the judgment of unfruitful lives.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus was baptized before John the Baptist began his ministry?
questions.explanation: According to Luke 3:21, Jesus was baptized after John had been preaching, marking a significant moment at the start of His ministry.

questions.question: Is it true that the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon Jesus during His baptism?
questions.explanation: This statement is true as per Luke 3:22, where the Holy Ghost is described as descending like a dove upon Jesus.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who was the son of Rhesa according to Luke 3:27?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Joanna, as stated in Luke 3:27, which lists Joanna as the son of Rhesa.

questions.question: Which individual is mentioned as the son of Levi in Luke 3:29?
questions.explanation: Matthat is identified as the son of Levi in Luke 3:29.

questions.question: In Luke 3:30, who is named as the son of Eliakim?
questions.explanation: Joseph is mentioned as the son of Eliakim in Luke 3:30.

questions.question: Which ancestor of Jesus is mentioned in Luke 3:31?
questions.explanation: David is noted as an ancestor in Luke 3:31, indicating Jesus' lineage.

questions.question: According to Luke 3:34, who was the son of Nachor?
questions.explanation: Abraham is identified as the son of Thara in Luke 3:34.

questions.question: In Luke 3:35, who is mentioned as the son of Sala?
questions.explanation: Heber is stated as the son of Sala in Luke 3:35.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'baptizo' in Luke 3:3 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Baptizo' means 'to immerse' in Greek, relating to the act of baptism in Luke 3:3.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Luke 3:4 with the phrase 'Prepare ye the way of the Lord'?
questions.explanation: The phrase foreshadows the coming of Jesus and the preparation needed for His ministry, as seen in Luke 3:4.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of baptism for repentance found in Luke 3:3?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:38 discusses baptism for repentance, echoing the theme in Luke 3:3.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the voice crying in the wilderness found in Luke 3:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:3 is a prophetic reference that connects to the voice crying in the wilderness mentioned in Luke 3:4.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Luke 3:27?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:26 precedes Luke 3:27 in the genealogy of Jesus.

questions.question: Which Greek word in Luke 3:6 refers to 'salvation'?
questions.explanation: 'Soteria' refers to salvation in Greek, as mentioned in Luke 3:6.

questions.question: In Luke 3:22, what does the voice from heaven proclaim?
questions.explanation: The voice from heaven declares, 'Thou art my beloved Son' in Luke 3:22.

questions.question: True or False: John the Baptist was imprisoned for reproving Herod, as stated in Luke 3:20.
questions.explanation: True, as Luke 3:20 states that Herod shut up John in prison for his reproving.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was baptized before John the Baptist began his ministry according to Luke 3:21.
questions.explanation: False, as Luke 3:21 indicates that Jesus was baptized during John's ministry, not before.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 3:3 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation requires baptism for the remission of sins
Salvation is by faith alone without repentance
Salvation is only for the Jews as God's chosen people
Salvation is dependent on fulfilling the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation requires baptism for the remission of sins
questions.explanation: Luke 3:3 emphasizes preaching 'the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins,' teaching that repentance and baptism are integral to the salvation process.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is taught in Luke 3:7?
options: Human sin provokes the coming wrath of God
Human sin is insignificant before God's patience
Human sin can be ignored if one is of Abraham's lineage
Human sin is only external and not internal
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin provokes the coming wrath of God
questions.explanation: Luke 3:7 records John calling the people 'a generation of vipers' and warning them to flee from the coming wrath, highlighting the reality and seriousness of human sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is presented in Luke 3:9?
options: God judges those who do not produce good fruit
God’s judgment is only symbolic and not actual
God’s judgment is reserved only for Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: God judges those who do not produce good fruit
questions.explanation: Luke 3:9 uses the metaphor of an axe laid to the root of trees, indicating that every tree not bearing good fruit will be cut down, teaching God's active judgment on unrighteousness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 3:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Luke 3:22, the voice from heaven declares 'Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased,' demonstrating God's attribute of divine approval and affirmation of Jesus' identity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by the phrase 'the word of God came unto John' in Luke 3:2?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:2 shows the initiative of God in revelation, demonstrating His sovereignty in directing history and speaking through John the Baptist.

questions.question: How does Luke 3:4-6 connect to Old Testament prophecy and the theme of salvation?
options: It fulfills Isaiah's prophecy about preparing the way for the Lord
It contradicts the prophetic tradition by introducing a new message
It ignores Old Testament prophecy in favor of Roman political context
It limits salvation to a select group of Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Isaiah's prophecy about preparing the way for the Lord
questions.explanation: Luke 3:4-6 directly quotes Isaiah to show John the Baptist's role in preparing the way for salvation, connecting Jesus’ ministry to prophetic fulfillment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Luke 3:21-22 make regarding Jesus' baptism?
options: It inaugurates Jesus’ public ministry and divine sonship confirmation
It replaces the need for Old Testament sacrifices
It denies Jesus’ humanity by focusing only on divinity
It shows Jesus’ repentance for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It inaugurates Jesus’ public ministry and divine sonship confirmation
questions.explanation: The baptism in Luke 3:21-22 opens heaven and confirms Jesus as God's beloved Son, marking the beginning of His redemptive work.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 3:8 and Luke 3:9 teach about repentance and fruitfulness?
options: True repentance produces worthy fruit, and failure results in judgment
Repentance is unnecessary if one is of Abraham’s lineage
Fruitfulness is a human effort without divine involvement
Judgment is unrelated to personal holiness
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance produces worthy fruit, and failure results in judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 3:8 commands 'fruits worthy of repentance,' and 3:9 warns that trees without good fruit will be cut down, linking repentance to sanctification and judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 3:16 and Luke 3:17 teach about Jesus' baptism and eschatological judgment?
options: Jesus baptizes with the Holy Spirit and fire to separate righteous from unrighteous
Jesus' baptism is only symbolic without real judgment
John's baptism is superior because it uses water
Eschatological judgment is deferred and optional
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus baptizes with the Holy Spirit and fire to separate righteous from unrighteous
questions.explanation: Luke 3:16 contrasts John’s water baptism with Jesus’ baptism by the Spirit and fire, and 3:17 describes the fan separating wheat and chaff, teaching final judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about repentance and social ethics is synthesized in Luke 3:11 and Luke 3:14?
options: Repentance must manifest in generosity, honesty, and non-violence
Repentance is a private act without social implications
Social ethics are unrelated to repentance
Repentance excuses exploitation if religious rituals are performed
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance must manifest in generosity, honesty, and non-violence
questions.explanation: Luke 3:11 urges sharing possessions, and 3:14 commands soldiers to avoid violence and false accusation, showing repentance's ethical expression.

questions.question: Skeptics claim John’s baptism in Luke 3:3-6 was merely symbolic and lacked divine authority. What does the text actually teach?
options: John’s baptism is divinely ordained to prepare the way for Christ and calls for true repentance
John’s baptism was a human invention with no connection to God's plan
John’s baptism replaces Jesus’ ministry entirely
John’s baptism was only for Jews and had no universal significance
questions.correctAnswer: John’s baptism is divinely ordained to prepare the way for Christ and calls for true repentance
questions.explanation: Luke 3:3-6 shows John preaching under divine authority, fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy, and emphasizing repentance for forgiveness, affirming divine origin and purpose.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic courage and authority is taught in Luke 3:19-20?
options: Prophetic witness confronts sin even at personal cost
Prophets avoid political issues to stay safe
Prophetic authority depends on popular approval
John compromised with Herod to avoid imprisonment
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic witness confronts sin even at personal cost
questions.explanation: Luke 3:19-20 shows John reproving Herod for sin and being imprisoned, illustrating the costly but faithful prophetic ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's action in Luke 3:6: 'And all flesh shall see the salvation of God'?
questions.explanation: Luke 3:6 teaches that God's salvation is universal, intended for 'all flesh,' demonstrating God's attribute of universality in salvation.

questions.question: How does Luke 3:23-38 contribute to the theological understanding of Jesus’ identity?
options: It situates Jesus in the Davidic lineage, affirming His messianic and human ancestry
It denies Jesus' human genealogy to emphasize only divinity
It traces Jesus’ ancestry to pagan kings, undermining His Jewish identity
It focuses solely on Joseph’s lineage excluding Mary’s
questions.correctAnswer: It situates Jesus in the Davidic lineage, affirming His messianic and human ancestry
questions.explanation: The genealogy in Luke 3:23-38 traces Jesus’ descent from David to Adam and God, affirming both His messianic role and true humanity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Luke 3:13 and Luke 3:14 regarding roles and ethics in society?
options: God calls all to ethical conduct according to their societal roles
Only religious leaders must be ethical; others are exempt
Ethics are irrelevant to publicans and soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: God calls all to ethical conduct according to their societal roles
questions.explanation: Luke 3:13 commands tax collectors to exact no more than appointed, and 3:14 instructs soldiers to avoid violence and false accusations, showing tailored ethical demands.
